question: GQ-001
subject: the only script that deletes had no test, and my first test was decoration
the_gap: enforce-log-retention.sh is the one script in this repo that removes data. Every other gate has a self-test case proving it fires. This had ZERO coverage — and it had already destroyed the archive it depends on.

my_first_attempt_was_decoration.the_test_that_mattered: deleted the script and re-ran — 5 of 6 still passed
my_first_attempt_was_decoration.why: four cases asserted things about sqlite and my own fixtures; they would pass on an empty repo
my_first_attempt_was_decoration.this_is_the_defect_i_removed_a_guard_for: a check that cannot detect its own target reads as coverage

the_rewrite.change: every case now drives the real script via LOG_DB_OVERRIDE and SLICE_OVERRIDE against temp fixtures
the_rewrite.why_overrides: a destructive path that can only be tested against the real database never gets tested
the_rewrite.proof: with the script deleted the result inverts — 5 passed becomes 5 FAILED

a_real_bug_the_new_test_found.symptom: cases 4 and 5 failed: the script evicted nothing and pruned nothing on a clean fixture
a_real_bug_the_new_test_found.cause: a leftover guard compared the refreshed slice against LIVE and refused at 1/5. After ANY successful eviction live and slice always differ — that is what an archive is.
a_real_bug_the_new_test_found.consequence: the script could never have deleted anything a second time. It had run once; the next run would have refused forever.
a_real_bug_the_new_test_found.fix: re-probe the slice directly — does it ANSWER — instead of asking whether it agrees with a source that has moved on

result.wired_into: gate-selftest.sh as a probe, and npm run retention:selftest
